name: Aaron and Israel at the golden calf
charge: Idolatry within weeks of the covenant
summary: While Moses was on the mountain receiving the law that forbade it, the people made a golden calf and worshipped it. The covenant was broken almost before the ink was dry.
offense: Not forty days had passed since they heard the voice from the mount. When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down, they gathered themselves together unto Aaron and said, up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him (Exodus 32:1). Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation turned, and it turned toward what it had carried out of Egypt: the spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left, and it corrupted them the moment the man was out of sight. Aaron's part is the heavier for who he was. He had seen every plague and stood before Pharaoh and been set apart to the priesthood, and he received the gold and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf, and they said, these be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt (Exodus 32:4). Then he built an altar before it and proclaimed, to morrow is a feast to the Lord (Exodus 32:5), which is the offence named in the second commandment performed under the name of the first. They rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play (Exodus 32:6), and the Lord's own verdict was given before Moses had seen any of it: they have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them (Exodus 32:8), and, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people (Exodus 32:9).
judgment: Moses ground the calf to powder and made them drink it. The Levites, called to the Lord's side, put about three thousand to the sword, and the Lord sent a plague on the people. Aaron was spared but not excused.

entries.commentary: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day. Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin. Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means. Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God. Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word. From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables. Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses. As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount. He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day.

Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness. Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried. The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3), the shame of sin uncovered. Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually. Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over Jordan this day, to possess nations greater and mightier than thyself, a people great and tall, the children of the Anakims, of whom it was said, who can stand before the children of Anak. The Anakims are Hamites, scattered now in the land of Ham; do not ask which nation they are today, for the Most High has not told us. The Lord thy God goeth over before thee as a consuming fire; he shall destroy them and bring them down before thy face, so shalt thou drive them out and destroy them quickly.

Speak not thou in thine heart, saying, for my righteousness the Lord hath brought me in to possess this land: here is more of the Christianity spirit corrected. Israel entered for the wickedness of those nations and to perform the word sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not for their own uprightness. Understand that the only reason any of us have a roof over our head and food in our stomach right now is the mercy and righteousness of the Most High, for thou art a stiffnecked people; it is because of him that we survive every single day.

Remember, and forget not, how thou provokedst the Lord thy God to wrath in the wilderness: from the day of leaving Egypt unto this place, ye have been rebellious against the Lord. Moses abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, when he went up to receive the tables of the covenant. What was he doing those forty days? He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times, and the end of times; that is why some things Moses wrote, like [Genesis 49](/bible/genesis/49) and [Deuteronomy 32](/bible/deuteronomy/32) and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy.

The Lord delivered unto me two tables of stone written with the finger of God: God took his time and wrote the ten commandments down himself, according to all the words which the Lord spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire.

Arise, get thee down quickly; thy people have corrupted themselves and made them a molten image. That molten image was the calf, the Egyptian goddess Hathor; you can look that up yourself. Let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven, and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they. The Most High was ready to go back to the days of the flood and start over with one man; time means nothing to the Ancient of days. Religion has tried to remove the fierceness, the wrath, and the severity of the Most High and push an effeminate white Jesus in front of us that loves everybody, forgives everything at the last breath with no commandments kept, and can do no wrong. We are suffering in all our cities, in Africa, in Europe, and in the Caribbean from that lack of fear of God before our eyes.

Moses came down from the mount, the mount burning with fire, the two tables of the covenant in his two hands, and behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God and made you a molten calf. Ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the Lord had commanded you: the Most High had been proving them through hard times, and they quickly turned back, just as many today go right back to their old ways the moment they are left alone. Brothers and sisters, check yourselves; we must endure to the end and rehearse the righteous acts now. Moses took the two tables, cast them out of his two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

Moses fell down before the Lord, as at the first, forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, because of all your sins; that is two forty-day fasts, for he was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure wherewith the Lord was wroth against the people. The Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him, and Moses prayed for Aaron also at the same time. Moses prayed, and the Lord hearkened unto him; there arose no prophet like Moses, a mighty great man in the scriptures. He took your sin, the calf which ye had made, burnt it with fire, stamped it, ground it very small until it was as small as dust, and cast the dust into the brook that descended out of the mount.

At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibrothhattaavah ye provoked the Lord to wrath, and at Kadeshbarnea ye rebelled against the commandment of the Lord and believed him not. Ye have been rebellious against the Lord from the day that I knew you: Moses called Israel out plainly, and it is real talk still.

Moses fell down before the Lord forty days and forty nights because the Lord had said he would destroy the people, and prayed: O Lord God, destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed through thy greatness. Remember thy servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, lest the land whence thou broughtest us out say the Lord was not able to bring them in, and because he hated them he brought them out to slay them. Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for the children of Israel, so precept these two prayers together: pay no attention to the fakers, for they remove themselves, but be merciful to us who have no works of righteousness, for by that mercy thou shalt be called merciful. When we are in the midst of sin we live worse than beasts, for a beast runs on instinct, but we consciously choose to go against the laws of the Most High.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

This is Stephen at the council, addressing the audience just before he is put to death. He answers the high priest by going all the way back to the beginning: the God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran. Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, dwelt in Charran, and after his father died the Most High removed him into this land wherein they now dwell, and gave him no inheritance in it, not so much as to set his foot on, yet promised to give it to him and his seed after him when as yet he had no child. Notice how Stephen recites this history off the top of his head. Our forefathers read more than their four chapters a day. When you read, you put these things to memory, so you can recite it. A lot of us cannot recite our own history, but we can recite LeBron James and the NBA stats, football stats. These men were studious; they constantly gave attendance to studying. They called Paul mad for reading so many letters. Our forefathers were addicted to this gospel.

The Most High spoke that Abraham's seed should sojourn in a strange land and be brought into bondage and treated evil four hundred years, and the nation to whom they were in bondage he would judge, and after that they would come forth and serve him in this place. Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt, but the Most High was with him and delivered him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, who made him governor over Egypt and all his house. When the famine came over Egypt and Canaan, Jacob heard there was corn in Egypt and sent out our fathers first; the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren, and Joseph's kindred was made known to Pharaoh. Jacob went down into Egypt with threescore and fifteen souls, and he and our fathers died and were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money.

As the time of the promise drew near which the Most High had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who knew not Joseph. The same dealt subtly with our kindred and evil-treated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children to the end they might not live.

In that time Moses was born, exceeding fair, nourished up in his father's house three months, and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son. Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was mighty in words and in deeds. That corrects the doctrine that certain Christian pastors preach, that Moses stuttered and could not speak. You cannot be a stupid man and be a prince over Egypt. He was raised under Pharaoh, so he had to learn everything of Egypt, their gods, their laws, the language. He was not a stupid man, and he did not stutter.

When Moses was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel. Contrary to the movie The Ten Commandments, Moses always knew who he was; his own mother raised and nursed him, so he knew his brothers, he was only raised under the household of the Egyptians. Seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him and smote the Egyptian, supposing his brethren would understand that the Most High by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not. The next day, striving to make peace, he was thrust away with, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? Only the Most High could set a man to judge. This is the crabs in a barrel spirit: even after you help somebody, they say, Who are you to be over us? Everybody wants to be the head, the chief, a leader, but nobody wants to be a follower, and nobody wants to give credit when credit is due. The Most High was using the status Moses had in Egypt to help his brother, and they used it against him: Wilt thou kill me as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday? Certain of us will be put in different positions in this society, in politics, in education, and the Most High will use those accolades to your advantage, the same way he used Moses to go to Pharaoh and not be put to death right off the bat. Then Moses fled and was a stranger in the land of Midian, understanding that if he stayed among his own people they would get him killed, and there he begat two sons. People use the excuse that Moses married an Ethiopian to justify interracial marriage, saying maybe the Lord would forgive them the same way. But the Most High says, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy. You are not Moses. Ask Aaron and Miriam, whom the Most High plagued in the skin and put out of the camp seven days for speaking against a matter that did not concern them. Do not point fingers and compare yourself to the person next to you, wondering why one brother is judged for a matter and another is treated differently. Different judgments belong to the Most High. You are not David; do not weigh Saul's sins against David's and assume you know how the Most High will judge, the way men questioned why Uzza was struck for touching the ark. Work out your own soul salvation with fear and trembling, study to be quiet, and mind your own business.

Forty years later, Moses now eighty years old, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush at Mount Sinai. Brothers and sisters say they are too old to repent; you are never too old. The Most High used Moses at eighty to deliver the whole nation, and retained his strength. The voice of the Lord said, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses trembled and durst not behold. He was told to put off his shoes, for the place was holy ground, and the Most High said, I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, I have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them; now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

This Moses, whom they refused saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge, the same did the Most High send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared in the bush. Be careful with one another; the same person you reject is the same person the Most High raises up over you. This is the spirit of preeminence, not wanting another brother to rule over you because you believe you should be in that position. The Most High sees the heart and knows the spirits he is setting up. Moses was the meekest, most humble man. For a prince to go down to people counted as slaves and servants, defend them, and risk himself for a stiffnecked and rebellious people, shows he loved his people even in his position of authority. This is that Moses who said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren like unto me; him shall ye hear. Stephen rehearsed all the history to bring them up to Christ, because the whole ministry throughout Acts is Christ's name preached in the place of animal sacrifice. Even as Pharisees, they knew this prophecy, so he made it plain: the prophet Moses spoke about is that Christ.

This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him in Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received the lively oracles to give unto us. The one in the church in the wilderness is that Christ, the prophet of verse 37. Our fathers would not obey him but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt, telling Aaron, Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses we know not what is become of him. They did not obey Christ in the wilderness, just as they did not obey Christ in his day. They made a calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands, so the Most High gave them up to worship the host of heaven; they took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Remphan, figures they made to worship, and he carried them away beyond Babylon.

Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, made according to the fashion Moses had seen, which our fathers brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom the Most High drove out before their face. That Jesus is Joshua, and the Most High drove out the nations before the fathers. This continued unto the days of David, who found favor before the Most High and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, but Solomon built him a house. Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool; what house will ye build me, saith the Lord, or what is the place of my rest? Hath not my hand made all these things?

Stephen turns it on them: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost; as your fathers did, so do ye. The Holy Ghost the fathers resisted in the wilderness is the same Holy Ghost resisted in Christ's day, and that Holy Ghost is first and foremost the laws. There are three forms of the Holy Ghost taught in this series: first the laws, when you keep the laws of the Most High; then wisdom and understanding, which comes after you keep the laws; and then power, as the apostles received power to speak in tongues and perform miracles. Which of the prophets did their fathers not persecute? They slew them that showed before of the coming of the Just One, of whom they had now been the betrayers and murderers, who received the law by the disposition of angels and kept it not.

When they heard these things they were cut to the heart and gnashed on him with their teeth. But Stephen, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of the Most High and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city, and stoned him; the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen, calling on the Most High, said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, and kneeling down he cried, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge, and fell asleep. This is the same spirit Christ had when he said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

verses.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.
And all the people brake off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.

And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To morrow is a feast to the Lord.
And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.
Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
And the Lord plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.
And I looked, and, behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God, and had made you a molten calf: ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the Lord had commanded you.
And I took the two tables, and cast them out of my two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

And I fell down before the Lord, as at the first, forty days and forty nights: I did neither eat bread, nor drink water, because of all your sins which ye sinned, in doing wickedly in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.
For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure, wherewith the Lord was wroth against you to destroy you. But the Lord hearkened unto me at that time also.
And the Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him: and I prayed for Aaron also the same time.

And I took your sin, the calf which ye had made, and burnt it with fire, and stamped it, and ground it very small, even until it was as small as dust: and I cast the dust thereof into the brook that descended out of the mount.
They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image.
Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.
They forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt;
Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.
Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.
To whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt,
Saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us: for as for this Moses, which brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.
Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

lawsResolved.text: I am the LORD your God, you shall have no other gods besides me.
You shall not make for yourself any carved image, or any likeness of anything; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them.
You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
Death penalty is to be given to idolaters.

text.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.
And all the people brake off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.

And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To morrow is a feast to the Lord.
And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.
Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
And the Lord plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.
And I looked, and, behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God, and had made you a molten calf: ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the Lord had commanded you.
And I took the two tables, and cast them out of my two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

And I fell down before the Lord, as at the first, forty days and forty nights: I did neither eat bread, nor drink water, because of all your sins which ye sinned, in doing wickedly in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.
For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure, wherewith the Lord was wroth against you to destroy you. But the Lord hearkened unto me at that time also.
And the Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him: and I prayed for Aaron also the same time.

And I took your sin, the calf which ye had made, and burnt it with fire, and stamped it, and ground it very small, even until it was as small as dust: and I cast the dust thereof into the brook that descended out of the mount.
They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image.
Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.
They forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt;
Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.
Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.
To whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt,
Saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us: for as for this Moses, which brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.
Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
